stock.counterargument: Growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +12.2%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $171.95 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 135 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 135 days before the decision date.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-12.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-25) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Learn With Mentor AI: Working Through a Coding Exercise
stories.excerpt: Learn how to use Mentor AI on a Real Python coding exercise. Ask why a test failed, get hints instead of the answer, and check your understanding.
stories.lead:
Real Python has hundreds of coding exercises that let you practice what you’ve learned in a tutorial or course. Each exercise gives you a task, a code editor, and a set of tests that check your solution. When all the tests pass, you’ve solved the exercise.

Sometimes, though, the tests keep failing and you can’t figure out why. At that point, it’s tempting to open the solution and copy it. The tests turn green, but you don’t learn much from it.

Tyler's opioid addiction began in his early 20s, and when he decided he wanted to quit, he used kratom leaf powders to help ease withdrawal symptoms.

Tyler, now 38, told NPR he thinks kratom helped him stop using opioids for a decade.

Tyler asked NPR to use only his first name because of the stigma attached to his history with drug use and addiction.

stories.title: Australian cricket's sandpapergate is back - and it cuts deep in a 'nation of good sports'
stories.excerpt: Claims the entire Australian team knew of the 2018 sandpaper cheating plot are dividing the cricket world.
stories.lead:
As Australian cricket captain Pat Cummins spent more than an hour being grilled by reporters over one of sport's biggest cheating scandals, the tension in the hall was occasionally pierced by muffled cheers.

Outside, a crucial match in the top tier of domestic cricket was getting under way. Cummins was clear he'd rather we all be talking about that.

But inside the nets at Cricket Central in Sydney, he faced more than a dozen TV cameras and a gaggle of journalists several times as large. His goal: to put rumours of his involvement in "sandpapergate" to rest.

stories.title: These two voter turnout trends explain what happened across the South in the election
stories.excerpt: In six states across the Deep South, a drastic swing to the left this election was driven by high Black voter turnout and compounded by a sharp decline in voting rates across Republican-heavy areas.
stories.lead:
Democratic victories in the South this year were driven just as much by who showed up to vote as who stayed home, according to an NPR analysis of turnout data.

Midterm elections normally have lower voter participation than presidential contests. But from Louisiana to the Carolinas, counties that voted for former Vice President Kamala Harris in 2024 came closer to matching — and in some cases exceeding — presidential turnout. At the same time, counties won by President Trump saw a much sharper decline in turnout and fewer Republican votes.

stories.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
stories.excerpt: As it races to develop its new massive rocket, the space launch company is preparing to retire NASA's main ride to the International Space Station.
stories.lead:
Later today, SpaceX is planning the most ambitious test yet of its massive new rocket Starship. If all goes well, it will lift off from a pad in South Texas, circle the Earth and then land vertically at the same pad 22 and a half hours later.

The test would be a major milestone for a rocket that company founder Elon Musk says he hopes will one day carry astronauts to Mars. But experts say the rapid development of Starship could also end up stranding one of the company's biggest boosters over the years: NASA.

stories.title: Hegseth awards medal to soldier who chastised him
stories.excerpt: Pete Hegseth was yelled at by a sentinel for poor decorum at Arlington National Cemetery. Now the Secretary of Defense has given him a medal.
stories.lead:
Coming out of the bruising the Republicans suffered in the midterms, this week was bearing up to be a bad one for Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. Many thought he'd be the first in the administration to be fired for his support of the Iran war, which proved unpopular with voters.

Then a member of his own party called for a vote to impeach him and, in an embarrassing incident that went viral, he also got chastised for poor decorum when visiting the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.

Still, he managed to survive the former – except for Thomas Massie, who sponsored the resolution to impeach him, all other Republicans in the House voted against it – and sought to turn the latter into a PR opportunity.

stories.title: Heat pumps: How much heat does your home really need?
stories.excerpt: Knowing how much heat your home loses is important before installing a new heating system.
stories.lead:
Floorplans. Air duct diagrams. Heat pump specifications. Most people in the market for a new heating system probably don't want to think about this level of detail.

But, perhaps surprisingly, some do want to think about those things. In extreme depth.

Every day, roughly 150 new users sign up to an app called Cool Calc, which works out the heat requirements of properties in the US.
